I reviewed all of lines 1–90 and applied only the "Repeated proof machinery" rubric. I did not search the other source roots, because the supplied text was enough to decide this.

The shared steps are already factored out. `dense_approx` gives a dense-sequence point within r of y. `choose_m` turns "for every x some dense-sequence index works, and each index gives a measurable set" into a measurable choice function. `near_m` gives measurability of the `near` sets.

`start` and `next` follow the same pattern: pick a witness, approximate it by a dense-sequence point, then call `choose_m`. What remains specific to each is small:
- In `start`, the witness is only in F, and the predicate is `near F x y (eps 0)`.
- In `next`, the predicate also includes `dist (x.val a) y ≤ 2*eps n`, so its measurability proof and triangle-inequality step are specific to it.

A further helper would only move these branches into another lemma, which the rubric says is insufficient.

The remaining repeats are short: `by unfold eps; positivity`, and the small `eps (n+1) = eps n/2` calculation. These are routine calculations and do not justify a shared lemma. The Cauchy-limit argument in `selector` appears only once.

I found no justified finding. I did not compile anything. The only uncertainty is that I did not check the rest of the project for further copies of this selection pattern.
